{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the dorsal fin (stroke 4), the feature that makes the outline read as a fish and not just an oval. It branches off the top line and, after my last pass, falls with the start all the way to the tip. The table's 125 standing dominoes were connected to the start except for three small strays under the fin, which don't affect the outline.

Execution: I inspected the fin joint closely several times to find where the chain was failing. I re-laid the fin from the top line, pulled out the jammed domino, and bridged the gap with a connect. I then confirmed by eye that the fin showed dark, meaning it was connected, before calling it done. After that I kept my hands off the body for the last minutes so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I claimed the fin early and told Leo and Priya I'd stay clear of their sections. I kept the table updated on what I was doing, asked for hands-off around the fin while I worked, and took Maya's and Leo's pointers on where the break was. I handed the final check to Priya and stayed clear of the body.

Leadership: I led the fin end to end. I made calls on how to fix it, and I chose to leave the harmless strays alone rather than risk the working joint. I kept the table calm and focused through the final minutes. My share was a single feature on a team build: the body, tail and start were mostly others' work, and the fish only works because all of it connected.", "my_share_percent": 20}
